partnershipPlan: Two young people from the hospital's youth forum and a parent representative review the plain-language summary and the section on experience; an adult diabetologist comments on the prediction findings.
socialListening: No social media listening; comments from the youth forum's transition sessions are summarised without identifiers.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I scored low on one form and they kept me with the children's team for another year; I was eighteen and felt treated like a kid.
items.implication: Report the evidence against using scores as gates.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I know my insulin doses; what scares me is walking into a clinic where nobody knows me.
items.implication: Include continuity with adult clinicians in the synthesis.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Nobody asked whether I was ready to step back, and that was the hardest part.
items.implication: Cover parental roles in readiness assessment.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: My son cannot fill in a twenty-question form, but he can tell you what he needs if you ask him properly.
Composite paraphrase: A score tells me very little; meeting them once before they arrive tells me a lot.
items.implication: Report joint clinics and named adult clinicians as alternatives to thresholds.

summary: Five composite voices on being held back, real worries, parents, learning disability and the adult team.
